source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-44

procedures.title: POA valve (evaporator control valve): replace
steps: Disconnect the battery ground cable and purge the refrigerant.
Disconnect the inlet, outlet, oil bleed and expansion valve lines and cap them at once.
Remove the screw holding the valve body bracket to the evaporator case (or case bracket) and take out the valve with its bracket.
Install the new valve in reverse order, then evacuate and charge the system.
notes: The valve cannot be repaired or adjusted; replace it if faulty.
See figure 49 in the manual for installation on each model.

procedures.title: Expansion valve: replace
steps: Before replacing, rule out other causes: bulb correctly placed on the low pressure line, clamped tight and insulated, and the liquid inlet screen (between valve and receiver-dehydrator line) not clogged.
Disconnect the battery ground cable and purge the system.
Unclamp the power element bulb from the low pressure line and disconnect the equalizer line from the POA valve.
Disconnect the low pressure connector, then the high pressure connector.
Remove the screw and bracket holding the valve to the blower or evaporator case and take the valve out.
Check the inlet screen; if plugged, replace it and recheck valve operation, and replace the valve only if it still misbehaves.
Connect the lines to the new valve, clamp its bulb on top of the low pressure line and connect the equalizer line to the suction throttling valve.
Refit the insulation around the bulb and make sure the bulb touches the suction line firmly.
notes: The valve is preset at the factory and cannot be adjusted.
Failure causes: needle stuck open or shut from corrosion, or a discharged power element from a broken capillary line or tip.

procedures.title: Vacuum tank: description
notes: Carburetor vacuum falls under hard acceleration; the vacuum tank, with a check valve, stores vacuum so the controls keep working.
On the Corvette there is no separate A/C vacuum tank (see next page).
